suitability_reason: Every decided issue (Schedule C car/truck, travel, other expenses) turns on substantiation and credibility under §§162, 274(d), 6001.

taxpayer.notes: Employed as school counselor (DISD) and insurance salesman (Liberty); Schedule C "business consultant" activity with no reported income. Pro se; failed to file brief.

adjustments: disallowed Schedule C car and truck expenses $22,499
conceded: Respondent: entitled to student loan interest deduction of $42
Parties agree remaining adjustments are computational

findings_of_fact.fact: 2018 wages from DISD and Liberty $78,180; Schedule C loss $49,202; refund claimed $5,991
findings_of_fact.snippet: On Schedule C Mr. Mitchell deducted $22,499 in car and truck expenses, $11,376 in travel expenses, and $8,984 in other expenses.

findings_of_fact.fact: Mileage log 81,186 business miles; inspection reports show 21,816 miles driven Oct 20, 2017-Nov 15, 2018
findings_of_fact.snippet: 21,816 miles were driven on the vehicle, far less than the driven miles shown on the mileage log.

findings_of_fact.fact: Court finds no mileage incurred for business purpose
findings_of_fact.snippet: the Court finds that no mileage was incurred for a business purpose.

findings_of_fact.fact: 20 hotel receipts totaling $2,635.19, found altered and not credible
findings_of_fact.snippet: The Court determines that the receipts have been altered and are simply not credible or reliable.
The Court sustained respondent’s objection and did not admit the receipts into evidence.

issues.question: Schedule C (§162/§274(d)): may petitioner deduct $22,499 of car and truck expenses?
issues.holding: No; mileage log unreliable, testimony not credible

issues.question: Schedule C: may petitioner deduct $11,376 of travel expenses?
issues.holding: No; receipts altered, strict substantiation not met

issues.question: Schedule C: may petitioner deduct $8,984 of other (advertising) expenses?
issues.holding: No; receipts not authenticated or admitted; no other substantiation

decision.text: Decision will be entered under Rule 155.
decision.summary: All disputed Schedule C deductions disallowed; respondent conceded penalty and $42 student loan interest

notes: Unsuitable: pure substantiation case. NOD issued December 28, 2020; trial January 24, 2022.
